rejected_reason: In b the generic inspector is placed in record scenes where the source gives her no role. At 11.6 to 13.8 s the EPA approval letter slides onto her desk, and from 16.8 to 19.6 s she raises a pen toward the letter while the Approved mark lands. Muted, this reads as the reviewer receiving or approving EPA's decision. From 19.8 to 21.6 s, during 'The drone carries an infrared camera', the drone is a tiny icon on a wall-mounted feed screen and the camera is not legible. The inspector sits idle facing right, and watching the live feed implies real-time review, while the letter describes review after the data are collected. She is also held in an unchanging pose at 11.6 to 13.8, 19.8 to 21.6 and 33.6 to 35.6 s. B's ending is stronger: the large empty AI box and pad window card are fully readable from 53.8 to 56.2 s. That alone does not outweigh the implied-role and hero-legibility costs.
